newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens 9-month net profit up 3 percent.
newsitem.headline: Siemens 9-month net profit up 3 percent.

text.p: German industrial group Siemens AG said Monday its profits in the first nine months of 1996/97 rose 3 percent to 1.705 billion marks ($953.8 million), thanks to positive currency effects and rising sales of computer communications equipment.

Sales in the period grew 10 percent to 71.2 billion marks ($39.6 billion), while orders rose 14 percent to 82.8 billion marks ($46 billion). Favourable currency rates accounted for two percentage points of sales growth and four percentage points of order growth, the company said.
"Buoyant business in the Americas and Asia-Pacific more than compensated for a light decline in Germany," Siemens said. "Growth was generated exclusively by international business."

The company stood by an earlier forecast of flat profits in 1996/97, despite the surprisingly strong results, saying that losses in its medical and transportation units and higher taxes would dampen earnings.
CEO Heinrich von Pierer told a news conference that profits would rise again in 1997/98.
Orders in North and South America rose 26 percent to 16.5 billion marks ($9.2 billion), including a 20 percent rise in U.S. business to 10.7 billion marks ($5.9 billion).
In Asia, orders climbed 45 percent to 11.5 billion marks ($6.4 billion), while European orders outside of Germany rose 13 percent to 20.2 billion marks ($11.2 billion).
Domestic orders fell 2 percent to 27.2 billion marks ($15.1 billion), while domestic sales slipped 1 percent to 24.9 billion marks ($13.8 billion).
Siemens also said capital spending and investments in the nine months to June 30 rose 28 percent to 6.3 billion marks ($3.5 billion).
In the nine-month period, Public Communications sales rose 28 percent to 9.9 billion marks ($5.5 billion), while Private Communications sales climbed 12 percent to 7.8 billion marks ($4.3 billion).
Computer unit Siemens-Nixdorf Informationssystems AG saw sales in the period rise 11 percent to 10.8 billion marks ($6 billion), while orders grew 13 percent to 11.6 billion marks ($6.4 billion).
Siemens semiconductor sales rose 20 percent to 4.1 billion marks ($2.3 billion) and orders increased 19 percent to 4.5 billion marks ($2.5 billion).
